messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency SLO breach detected on serving cluster 'eu-west-2-gpupool-3'. Auto-page sent to oncall. Investigate and update.

carmen: on it. seeing big jump in p95/p99 across chat/generate routes. streaming stalls too. grabbing dashboards.

carmen: quick metrics snapshot — p95 from ~120ms -> ~560ms, p99 from ~420ms -> ~2.6s. streaming stall rate (partial responses) went from 1.2% -> 13%.

raj: I can repro on staging-ish by replaying a subset. Looks correlated with KV cache eviction spikes on shard set a1,a2. eviction_rate/sec spiked ~x6 around 13:02 UTC.

raj: suspecting KV fragmentation + prefill vs decode imbalance. prefill workload creating many small entries, decode path misses more often after eviction leading to long tail as we rebuild KV for streaming requests.

dina: logging shows prefill insertion rate increased due to a burst of long-context customers. KV free pages fragmented, compaction not keeping up.

carmen: are specific customers affected? any enterprise traffic in that region? need to scope.

raj: early filter shows 3 high-traffic tenants (tenant-A, tenant-B, tenant-C) accounted for ~48% of evictions. non-streaming generate routes less impacted. streaming-heavy routes hit tail the worst.

sara: infra note — memory fragmentation observed on host-level. compaction job lagging behind due to CPU contention from background quantization job (recent deploy).

carmen: immediate mitigation suggestions?

raj: short-term options:
- increase KV eviction_threshold on a1/a2 from 0.85 -> 0.93 to reduce eviction churn
- temporarily disable prefill for non-critical tenants (tenant-A/B) to lower write churn
- route streaming requests for affected tenants to smaller-model variant (reduced cache footprint)
- fallback: disable streaming (switch to non-streaming chunked responses) for impacted routes to avoid stall behavior

carmen: can we try increasing eviction_threshold first (safer) and monitor?

sara: I can push threshold bump to a1/a2 now. will watch memory usage.

sara: Command I'm running:
```
platform-cli kv update --shards a1,a2 --eviction-threshold 0.93 --reason "incident mitigation"
```

sara: pushed. monitoring...

raj: while that's rolling, I'll prepare a per-tenant prefill kill switch. simple toggle at routing layer to drop prefill ops for tenant-A/B.

linus: heads-up — the threshold bump will increase memory tail for a bit, might trigger OOM if compaction doesn't catch up. keep eye on host OOM counts.

carmen: noted. ramping alert thresholds for mem/OOM to avoid noise.

(some minutes pass)

sara: threshold bump applied to both shards. eviction_rate dropped ~40% within 30s. p95 improved to ~210ms, p99 down to ~820ms. streaming stall rate down to ~5.6%.

carmen: great improvement. any regressions?

linus: memory usage increased ~7% on those hosts. compaction not yet fully caught up but acceptable for now.

raj: going to flip prefill kill for tenant-A as a precaution. toggling:
```
routing-cli set-prefill --tenant tenant-A --enabled false
```

raj: flipped. monitoring request success and latency.

carmen: good. request rates stable. p99 for tenant-A dropped to ~480ms. overall p99 now ~650ms.

incident-bot: NOTE: Customer-impact tag added — "partial-responses". Pager duty: oncall escalation remains.

carmen: handoff plan — I'm oncall for 30m, then handing to @raj for next 4 hours. if things look stable after 30m we'll coordinate long-term fixes.

raj: taking handoff at +30. action items I'm leaving for myself:
- run kv compaction sweep on a1/a2 with throttling
- schedule a targeted compaction job for heavily-fragmented pages (non-blocking)
- implement per-tenant prefill quotas (short-term soft-limits)
- postmortem draft with root-cause analysis (prefill burst -> fragmentation -> eviction churn -> decode misses)

dina: logging note: collected heap/kv snapshots and decoder cache hit/miss traces for the window (13:00-13:20). storing in incident bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/3401236789/

carmen: customer comms: ops to draft a brief note to tenants that saw partial responses. Tier-1 customers flagged.

sara: adding a safety runbook entry: if p99 > 1s and eviction_rate > baseline x3, then auto-bump eviction_threshold + disable prefill for top-evict tenants. need product sign-off but doable.

carmen: temporary mitigation worked. moving to monitoring/handoff. keep thread updated with any regression.

raj: handover: taking over now. I will kick off compaction + soft quotas. leaving prefill toggles for tenant-B/C if needed.

raj: running async compaction job now (throttled). command:
```
infra-cli compaction start --shards a1,a2 --rate-limit 50mbps --window 2h --reason "incident 3401236789"
```

(about 45m later)

raj: compaction progressed ~60% on targeted pages. fragmentation metric improved ~35%. eviction rate stabilized near baseline. p95 ~150ms, p99 ~220ms, streaming stalls ~1.6%.

dina: collecting data for postmortem. preliminary root cause: sustained prefill write burst from long-context sessions + background CPU contention from a recent quantization job which starved compaction. both combined to cause fragmentation and eviction churn.

carmen: marking incident as mitigated. not fully recovered to steady-state but within SLO.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Mitigation achieved. Next steps: postmortem + follow-ups. Severity: Sev2 -> downgraded.

raj: follow-ups:
- ticket INFRA-1289: add compaction backpressure for CPU-heavy jobs
- ticket SERVE-4570: per-tenant prefill quotas + admin kill-switch in console
- ticket TELE-902: add telemetry for prefill/decode imbalance alerts (ratio metric)

carmen: thanks all. I'll open the postmortem draft and share for review. cc @product-security for customer comms. :thumbsup:

sara: thumbs up. moving to cleanup. will rollback eviction_threshold to planned target after compaction finishes if safe.

linus: nice work on the mitigation sequence.

(incident thread closed for real-time ops)
